thesis_summary: Short SBUX vs long RSPD. The market has pre-paid for the Niccol turnaround — SBUX trades at the 76th percentile of its 52-week ratio vs the equal-weight sector while US comps and traffic remain negative and margin investment lands before revenue inflects. We are short the gap between turnaround narrative and turnaround data.
thesis_detail: SBUX is +12.0% over 1Y and +8.3% over 6M, the strongest relative performer in our coverage (RS vs XLY +6.7% over 63 days), yet the fundamental inflection the multiple capitalizes has not appeared in the data. US company-operated comps have been negative on traffic for over a year, and the 'Back to Starbucks' plan front-loads costs — incremental labor hours, Green Apron service rollout, store uplifts — meaning restaurant-level margin compresses in the quarters before any comp benefit shows. Consensus is modeling a 2H comp inflection and paying ~mid-30s forward earnings for it; every print showing transactions still negative forces estimate cuts into a premium multiple. The pair ratio (SBUX/RSPD) at 1.797 sits at the 76th percentile of its 52-week range (1.371–2.069) with a +0.89 z-score — the sector-relative premium is near cycle highs while the fundamental delivery is at cycle lows. Technicals corroborate stalling momentum: price below the 20dma, MACD histogram negative, OBV falling, volume at 0.51x 20-day average — the rally is losing participation at rich relative levels. Note: pair-ratio module last stamped 2026-07-28; returns data is fresh (1D prints), ratio treated as current within tolerance. Valuation snapshot endpoint was rate-limited (429) this session, so multiples are from model knowledge, flagged as such.
variant_perception: Consensus treats the comp inflection as a matter of timing and pays for it today; we see a value-perception and service-model problem where traffic recovery lags the cost build by at least two quarters, making the next two prints asymmetric to the downside for the relative premium.
catalyst: Fiscal Q4 print (late Oct/early Nov) plus interim high-frequency card data showing US transactions still negative; guidance on FY27 margin trajectory embedding full labor investment.
key_risks: Comp inflection arrives early — a positive US traffic print squeezes the premium wider, not narrower; ratio stop is just below the 52w high for this reason
Technical score is 8/bullish with a golden cross intact — we are shorting a stalled uptrend, not a confirmed downtrend; early entry risk is real
